A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UPD/MM-UPD study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison, including content relocated or renumbered in v4.

before.justification: V2 reports original LMM evaluations, prompting and fine-tuning experiments, ablations, and error analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds an option-order variability experiment in Appendix B.5 and Table D.

M1.justification: Benchmark construction, refusal prompts, answer extraction, chain-of-thought, self-reflection and LoRA tuning remain unchanged. The fine-tuning recipe summarized in v4 Section 5.5 already appears in v2 Appendix D.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MM-UPD coverage: 820 AAD, 919 IASD and 356 IVQD questions. Both also include the 459-question MMMU-AAD experiment and A-OKVQA training data. The added option-order analysis uses existing coverage.

E2.justification: The model roster and comparator membership in retained experiments are unchanged. The new variability analysis uses four already-evaluated LMMs and introduces no new competing method.

E3.justification: V4 Appendix B.5 adds an auxiliary evaluation measuring accuracy separately under three shifted answer-option patterns. It repeats Pattern 2 for two-choice questions in Pattern 3. The main circular-evaluation protocol, datasets and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 adds a targeted option-order sensitivity analysis comparing variability across AAD, IASD and the smaller IVQD set for four LMMs. Existing bottleneck analyses, tuning ablations, metric comparisons and error examples are retained.

E5.justification: Table D newly reports mean-plus/minus variability summaries and three individual pattern scores. These measure variation across answer orders, rather than independent seeds or training runs. The meaning of the plus/minus statistic is not explicitly defined.

E6.justification: V4 Table D adds 12 model/task summaries, including GPT-4o IVQD Base at 70.60 ± 1.08 across option shifts. Tables 1–3 and the existing appendix results retain their values. The new results use a separate protocol and do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The UPD task definitions and mathematical treatment of Dual and Original Conditional Dual accuracy are unchanged. V4 adds no theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, three stated contributions and conclusion retain their meaning and scope. The separately headed finding about larger open-source models and the new main-text fine-tuning summary restate findings already present in v2.

C2.justification: V2 Appendix B.4 defends IVQD's size through observed performance differences. V4 B.4–B.5 adds the argument that low option-order variability supports dataset-size sufficiency. The fine-tuning tradeoff with general-purpose performance, repeated in Section 5.5, was already discussed in v2 D.3.

D1.justification: V4 documents the new analysis's pattern-duplication rule and two-choice proportions: 10.1% for AAD, 1.85% for IASD and 8.7% for IVQD. Existing hardware, decoding, tuning information and resource-access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds citations to Onohara et al. (2025) on JMMMU and Noda et al. (2025) on real-world out-of-distribution detection. These modestly update the literature coverage without changing the paper's established positioning.

P1.justification: V4 adds a main-text summary of existing fine-tuning findings, separates the large-model finding into F3, and adds a bottleneck-analysis heading. Terminology, author information and acknowledgments receive limited edits; most prose and the overall organization are retained.

P2.justification: V4 adds the variability Table D, makes small alignment and icon changes to Figure 1, moves Figure 5 within page 8, and reflows appendix displays. Existing plots and detailed result tables retain their substantive visual structure.

improvement.justification: The added option-order experiment and individual pattern scores modestly strengthen empirical scrutiny, while Section 5.5 makes existing tuning tradeoffs easier to find. The gain is limited: three patterns, including duplicated two-choice cases, provide an order-stability check but do not establish sampling uncertainty or dataset-size adequacy as the discussion suggests. The central evidence remains unchanged.
